questions.question:
**Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.**

A system of government in which power is held by the people
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Democracy"**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning of given words.
 
• **Bureaucracy: **a system of government in which most of the important decisions are taken by state officials rather than by elected representatives.
 
• **Autocracy: **a system of government by one person with absolute power.
 
• **Democracy: **a system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.
 
• **Monarchy: **a form of government with a monarch(King or Queen) at the head.
 
• The given sentence is closest to the meaning of the word **democracy**.
 
 
• **Example**: *India is one of the biggest **democracies**__ in the world*.
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is option 3**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] __Hinglish__** 

__
 
• आइए दिए गए शब्दों के अर्थ को देखें।
 
• **नौकरशाही(bureaucracy)**: सरकार की एक प्रणाली जिसमें अधिकांश महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय राज्य के अधिकारियों द्वारा लिए जाते हैं, न कि निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधियों द्वारा।
 
• **लोकतंत्र(democracy)**: पूरी आबादी या राज्य के सभी पात्र सदस्यों द्वारा आम तौर पर निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधियों के माध्यम से सरकार की एक प्रणाली।
 
• **राजशाही(monarchy)**: सिर पर एक सम्राट (राजा या रानी) के साथ सरकार का एक रूप।
 
• **निरंकुशता(autocracy)**: पूर्ण शक्ति वाले एक व्यक्ति द्वारा सरकार की व्यवस्था।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य लोकतंत्र शब्द के अर्थ के सबसे करीब है।
 
 
• **उदाहरण**: भारत दुनिया के सबसे बड़े लोकतंत्रों में से एक है।

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

We received all the health updates but were not sure __whether its accurateness__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**about their accuracy**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous part of the sentence is '**whether its accurateness**'.
 
• We use whether in a sentence when there is a choice or alternative between two things.
 
 
• **Example**: *She asked me **whether **__I wanted eggs for breakfast or not.*
 
 
 
• We use **about **as a **preposition **in a sentence when we are about to discuss a subject (something or someone).
 
• In the given sentence we are talking about health updates and their accuracy so we can use **about **in the sentence.

**The correct sentence is: ***We received all the health updates but were not sure ***__*about their accuracy*.__**

**Hence, the correct answer is option 3**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

You have to submit a copy of_______ school leaving certificate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**your**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, we have to use a **possessive adjective**.
 
• **Possessive adjectives **are used when we have to show who or what **owns something**.
 
• Examples of the possessive adjective: **are my, our, your, his, her, its, and their**.
 
• Possessive adjectives **are used before nouns** in a sentence to modify the noun.
 
• Here the word **school **is a **noun **so we need to use 'your' to show possession.

**The complete sentence is**: *You have to submit a copy of** your__** school leaving certificate*.

**Hence, the correct answer is option 4**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** 

__
 
• There are also possessive pronouns such as are **mine, ours, yours, his, hers, its, and theirs**
 
• **Possessive pronouns **are used to show possession of a noun by replacing it.
 
• They are stand-alone and can be used without a noun.
 
 
• **Example**:* Aaditya's car is older than **mine**__.*

The correct answer is "**on**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence we need the preposition** on as there is a date(Friday) **after that blank.
 
• Prepositions such as on, at, and in are also known as** prepositions of time.**
 
• The preposition 'on' is used to refer **to a specific date or a day.**
 
 
• **Example: ***The new blockbuster movie is supposed to release **on **__Friday of this week.*
 
 
 
• The preposition 'at' indicates **the specific time**.
 __
 
• **Example**: *Ram is meeting me **at **__6 pm*
 
 
 
• The preposition 'in' indicates **the month, season, and year centuries.**
 __
 
• **Example: ***Ricky planned to inaugurate his new toy store** in **__December.*
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is option 3**

**The complete passage is:* ****Delhi recorded a spell of light rain **(1) on** Friday evening with humidity levels remaining on the higher side throughout** (2)** **the **day. The IMD has forecast moderate rain on Saturday but some areas **(3) are expected** to get heavy rain. An official also said that the next seven days are **(4)** **likely **to see good rain. The municipal corporation has been advised to remain prepared for water logging in **(5) low-lying** areas of the city.*
